unit: CH-02 refresh continuity - RC1, RC7-articles, RC2 and RC3
contract: REFRESH IS NOT NAVIGATION — reloading on a legitimate destination must reconstruct that destination (founder-frozen).
method: Executed against the existing shared-cause audit (docs/2026-08-17-refresh-continuity-shared-causes.md), which ranks nine root causes and orders the widest-leverage corrections. Corrections 1 and 7 were taken; the audit was not re-derived.

RC1.auditFinding: Web session restore gated behind a device-local hint boolean. The hint was written by only two sign-in paths, destroyed on transient refusal, and lost when SharedPreferences throws — every downstream gate then fired correctly against a FALSE unauthenticated premise.
RC1.alreadyFixedBeforeThisPass: The WRITE half. The hint is now written inside TokenStore.setSession — the choke point every authentication path funnels through — and cleared in clearTokens. Verified in code before assuming the audit was still current.
RC1.whatRemained: The READ half. `hasSessionHint()` collapsed three different facts into one boolean: a session existed, no session ever existed, and THIS BROWSER WILL NOT ANSWER. Private browsing makes SharedPreferences throw, so 'I cannot know' was being read as 'definitely never signed in' — and the restore was skipped for a signed-in person on every reload.
correction: SessionHintStatus tri-state — present / absent / unavailable — with readSessionHintStatus(). `unavailable` is never treated as `absent`.
A pure decision function, decideWebSessionRestore(status, landingPath), so the rule is testable without a browser, a router or a clock.
The hint stays an OPTIMISATION applied only where it was ever justified: a fresh tab landing on a genuinely public page. Everywhere else Aura asks.
RC1.theRuleNow: Restore is attempted unless the hint is definitively absent AND the landing path classifies PUBLIC (and is not the router's own /_boot). Cost of asking wrongly: one 401 in the console. Cost of skipping wrongly: a person loses their place.
RC1.unknownRoutesFailTowardAsking: classifyRoute already fails closed to MEMBER, so an unclassified route (RC6's gap, untouched here) costs a speculative refresh rather than a lost destination.
RC1.identityCeremoniesProtected: /complete-identity and /verify-pending classify AUTH_ACTION, not PUBLIC, so a reload mid-ceremony now restores instead of stranding the person.
RC1.hygieneWinPreserved: The original reason for the hint — no blind `401 Missing refresh token` on /, /public, /privacy, /mission, /login — is kept exactly, and a test asserts that EVERY skip in the whole decision space is that one case.

RC7.auditFinding: Draft surfaces never write identity into the URL. The Article editor called createDraft() on EVERY mount of /articles/write and never replaced the URL with /articles/write/<id>.
RC7.consequence: A reload did not reopen the article being written — it minted ANOTHER empty draft and left the real work unreachable, one orphan row per refresh. This is also the founder-reported 'draft not resumable' defect.
RC7.correction: On creating a draft the editor now context.replace()s to NavigationAuthority.articleEditorRoute(id). `replace`, not `push`: the id-less address was never a place worth going back to, and Back should leave the editor rather than return to a route that would mint yet another draft.
RC7.scope: The ARTICLE half only. The Compose half of RC7 (compose_screen's in-memory _draftPostId) is untouched and remains owed.
RC7.authorityReused: NavigationAuthority.articleEditorRoute — the canonical builder, which the audit noted existed and was simply unused here.

deliberatelyNotDone.RC4: One governed gateRedirect for destructive exits. NOT absorbed: RC2/RC3's contract does not necessarily own it, and preserving a ?redirect= the gate screens do not yet consume would be inert. Remains the next coherent step.
deliberatelyNotDone.RC5_RC6_RC8_RC9: Not attempted. Recorded as remaining, not dropped.
deliberatelyNotDone.RC7_compose_half: Remaining, under its own ownership - the article solution is not to be copied blindly across unrelated composers.

filesChanged: aura_final/lib/router.dart (both institution redirect helpers migrated onto the authority)

stateTransitions.F059: OPEN - unchanged. RC1, RC2 and RC3 corrected; RC4 remains, and the conversation-destination half still needs its own certification.
stateTransitions.F062: OPEN - unchanged. RC2 and RC3 were its named causes and are corrected; RC4 remains, as does the AUTHORIZED_ELSEWHERE screen-binding half of RC3.
stateTransitions.F063: OPEN - unchanged. Article surface corrected; compose surface (RC7's other half) and RC8 remain.
stateTransitions.honesty: NO finding is claimed closed or advanced. Root-cause repairs are recorded separately from finding closure, exactly as the register requires.

verification.frontendSuite: 704 PASS (675 before this chapter's work; 685 after RC1/RC7)

protectedBoundaries.meetings: UNTOUCHED — no meeting route, guard or session path modified
protectedBoundaries.guestSessions: UNCHANGED — guest tokens still deliberately do not write the hint

RC2.auditFinding: Route-level redirects run without the top-level still-resolving discipline: _redirectShorthandToCanonical read institutionIdentityProvider synchronously and, while it was still loading, six institution shorthand routes hard-landed on the dashboard. Cold-load of /institution/edit-profile could never survive.
RC2.rootCauseTraced: institutionIdentityProvider is a SYNCHRONOUS view over an ASYNC source - it reads institutionAccessProvider.valueOrNull and returns null. That null collapses three different facts: still loading, no affiliation, no access. The route redirects read it as the second. The top-level redirect already had the right discipline (it returns null while institution access loads on institution paths); the ROUTE-level redirects did not, and they run after it.
RC2.correction: InstitutionAuthoritySnapshot keeps resolved-ness separate from what is held, and UNRESOLVED is a first-class outcome. A canonical route expresses decide-nothing literally - return null, stay put, let the screen show its own loading state; the router re-runs redirects when the provider settles. A shorthand route has no builder and must resolve to an address, so it parks on the EXISTING destination-preserving /_boot?redirect= decision point that F068 already governs.
RC2.noRaceHiding: No timers, no delays, no retry loops, no polling. The only new state is a distinction that already existed in the AsyncValue and was being discarded.
RC2.errorIsNotLoading: An error is RESOLVED-but-unknown, not still-loading. Parking forever on a failed load would replace a lost destination with an eternal spinner, which F068 forbids; it falls through to the governed fallback.

RC3.auditFinding: Provider identity outranks the URL: _enforceCanonicalIdMatch rewrote any path id that disagreed with the active identity to the active one. Refreshing on institution B delivered institution A.
RC3.correction: The path id is now a CLAIM, validated against the memberships the backend reports (access.memberships[], the per-institution source C1 built). Only a validated claim is honoured. A stale, removed, unknown or foreign id is NOT silently swapped for whichever institution happens to be active - it goes to the governed dashboard, because quietly showing someone a different institution than the one they asked for is a truthfulness defect, not a convenience.
RC3.notAnAuthority: This does not make the path an authority. It makes the path a claim that resolved membership either supports or refuses - the same discipline ActingContextAuthority applies to acting identity (a path can never make someone an institution). Group identity doctrine was consumed, not re-decided.
RC3.honestLimitationNamed: AUTHORIZED_ELSEWHERE - the path names an institution the person genuinely holds but NOT the one the workspace is bound to. The four canonical workspace screens (profile, edit-profile, domains, request-verification) read the AMBIENT institution identity, so proceeding would render one institution's data under another institution's URL - a worse defect than the rewrite it replaces. The router therefore still canonicalises this case, but it is now a NAMED, TESTED outcome with its cause recorded rather than an accident. The remaining half of RC3 is: bind those screens to the URL's institution (per-institution capabilities already exist on MemberAffiliation) and provide an institution context to switch into. RECORDED AS OWED, not faked.

canonicalAuthorityIntroduced.shape: One pure decision - decideInstitutionRoute(snapshot, pathId) - over the outcomes unresolved / proceed / canonicalize / authorizedElsewhere / notAuthorized / noAffiliation, plus two pure mappers for the two route shapes.
canonicalAuthorityIntroduced.whyNotElevenPatches: The eleven institution route families were manifestations of ONE authority defect. Patching each redirect callback would have multiplied the defect's surface. Equally, one route god-function was avoided: the decision is shared, the composition is per-shape.
canonicalAuthorityIntroduced.routesUnchanged: Families that already pass institutionId into their screens (units, public-engagement and its children) were left alone - they never had the defect.
